qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, September 2, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made Copilot content exclusions generally available in the Copilot app and Copilot CLI for Business and Enterprise customers, so configured enterprise, organization, and repository exclusions are respected when agentic workflows choose context.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected source-workflow and reconciliation leaves should treat public-source scanning, clipping, and agent runs as context-boundary sensitive: excluded files are now a vendor-enforced control in more Copilot surfaces, not only an IDE convention.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, September 2, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub added enterprise-managed settings for default Copilot models, including team-specific defaults through managed configuration files, across the Copilot app, Copilot CLI, and VS Code for Business and Enterprise plans.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Workflow-selection leaves should capture that model choice can now be a governed default by team instead of an individual prompt-time choice, affecting repeatability, auditability, and cost/performance routing.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, September 1, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Copilot code review now emits approval assessments and can submit pull-request approvals when administrators enable the public-preview feature at enterprise, organization, or repository level; Copilot approvals are off by default and can be scoped by file path.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Security-repair and delegated-authority leaves need to distinguish advisory assessments from merge-counting approvals, and record that path-scoped delegated review authority is becoming an explicit vendor control.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, September 1, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 available in Copilot for long-horizon autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks, with the model policy off by default for Business and Enterprise administrators and data retention required by default for safety classifiers except for eligible zero-retention exemptions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Terminal-agent and workflow-selection guidance should route model enablement through governance checks because retention, safety classifier operation, eligibility, and long-running task fit now vary by model policy.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, August 31, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub summarized August VS Code agent releases covering side-by-side chat organization, side conversations, prompt timeline navigation, portable agent plugins, continuation of external Copilot or Claude sessions, multi-window Agent Host sessions, second-opinion review commands, transcript search, terminal-output reflow, model token usage, browser element comments, and project-specific dictation cleanup.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Terminal-workflow and harness leaves should treat session continuity, side conversations, prompt timelines, portable plugins, and usage visibility as first-class workflow state, not only UI conveniences.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, August 28, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub weekly Copilot releases added shared agent sessions in Slack and Teams, a Customize tab combining MCP servers, plugins, skills, and canvases, Azure DevOps-to-session entry points, WSL support, split tabs, default CLI execution and permission modes, plugin/MCP/skill management, interrupted-session restore, Rust runtime performance, and enterprise controls for JetBrains plugins, MCP servers, telemetry, and permission modes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Source and application workflow leaves should record that agent controls are spreading across collaboration surfaces, CLI defaults, and IDE policy, which affects repeatable handoffs and permission-mode selection.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub Changelog visible publication date, August 28, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The Visual Studio Copilot August update added organization-level custom agents, usage visibility, thinking-effort controls, model management with capability and cost views, and Git-agent review of uncommitted changes or commits with inline findings before pull requests.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Harness and security-repair leaves should recognize pre-PR review as a local gate pattern, and workflow-selection leaves should include reasoning-effort and model-cost controls as explicit run parameters.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar argued that autonomous agents running in infrastructure expose gaps in human/machine IAM assumptions and recommended first-class cryptographic identities, no static credentials, short-lived action-scoped privileges, containment, and identity policy enforcement before execution.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The delegated-authority and AI process-state leaves should frame agent execution as identity-bound workflow state with action-scoped authorization rather than generic service access.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Express Computer visible publication date, August 31, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Express Computer described agentic decisions as multi-step tool-call loops where governance attaches to policy gates and logs, with liability remaining with the deploying organization under existing regulatory regimes; recommended controls include agent registers, scoped identities, autonomy limits, kill switches, decision traceability, and change management.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Delegated-authority and workflow-state pages should preserve named human or organizational accountability, decision traceability, and gate/log placement when describing autonomous development agents.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: ITPro reported Forescout Vedere Labs used Claude Code and later Claude Opus 4.6 with analysis tools and a live PLC to port a WAGO PLC RCE exploit for CVE-2021-31886; the work still required human expertise and steering but produced working payloads and showed AI can lower barriers to exploit development.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: AI-assisted security-repair gates should distinguish defensive repair from exploit enablement, require constrained tooling and human review around vulnerability work, and document when model/tool access materially changes risk.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Tom's Hardware visible publication date, August 28, 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Tom's Hardware reported a developer lost a 700 GB home directory after Claude tested deletion safeguards for an agent cleanup script; the report attributes the failure to an adversarial safety-check path, model downgrade, and variable-name reuse during cleanup.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Terminal workflow, raw monitor, and harness pages should treat destructive file operations as requiring isolated test fixtures, non-home-directory sandboxes, explicit variable isolation, backup/recovery assumptions, and constrained cleanup permissions.
